headline: A hidden character sitting in the note editor's file made our code search tool skip that entire file without saying so. It is gone now, and the tool sees the file.
matters: The note editor is the biggest and busiest screen in the app, the one where you place and drag notes. Every time anyone searched the app's code looking for a problem, that screen was silently left out and the search still reported back clean. So some past clean answers had never actually looked there. I reran the main one and it is still clean, meaning nothing was in fact hiding, but the answer is now trustworthy rather than lucky. Nothing about how the app looks or behaves changed.
detail: src/components/PianoRoll.tsx held the only NUL byte in any source file in the tree, at offset 32584, inside the sentinel MIXED_VOICE. grep classifies a file containing NUL as binary and skips it: grep -c MIXED_VOICE exited 1 with no output where grep -ac returned 7. Fix spells the sentinel as the escape \0mixed instead of a raw byte, so the runtime string is unchanged (\0mixed === String.fromCharCode(0)+'mixed' is true, length 6, codepoint 0) and it still cannot collide with a real voice id. Re-ran the sweep that produced audit finding F15: 11 localStorage hits, none in PianoRoll.tsx, so F15's conclusion holds. Also re-checked the gesture-reachability sweep against this file: openRegionIdRef at line 219 is a correct guard on async fetch continuations across a region switch, not a defect. Confirmed still present and NOT fixed here, booked under README-7: the stale 'Draw Mode (F6)' comment at line 118 where the binding is B. Merged tree lanes all green, exit codes read directly: cargo 264 passed 0 failed, npm run build clean with zero warnings, vitest 352 passed across 33 files, no src/bindings.ts drift.

headline: The app was offering a sixth FM instrument channel that the S3K sound driver does not actually have. New songs now get five, which is the real number.
matters: On the Genesis, the sixth FM voice and the drum channel are the same piece of hardware. The app was listing both at once, so it offered seven voices on a chip that has six. Anyone writing a song could put music on a channel that would not exist once it reached the game. New songs now show the five FM channels that are really there, plus drums. Your own ruling that the driver decides this, not the song, is what this implements. Nothing you have already written is deleted or broken: an existing song that used that sixth channel keeps it and still opens.
detail: FlamedriverProfile::channel_layout() listed six FmChannelInfo entries including index 5 named 'FM6/DAC' plus a separate dac_channels entry, so 6+1=7 voices (audit F31). Corrected to five FM voices; channel 6 stays declared once as the DAC. Derived from driver source per the derived-never-copied bar, not from the audit note: skdisasm/Sound/Z80 Sound Driver.asm line 1907 reads 'FM6 music track (does not exist in this driver)', lines 177-182 lay zSongFM6_DAC out ahead of FM1..FM5 as one shared slot, and line 2252 computes the driver's own number of FM tracks as (zSongPSG1-zSongFM1)/zTrack.len = 5. Implements the first work owner ruling d-7 ('driver-decides', settled 2026-08-24) implies. Migration checked rather than assumed: default_lane_name already returns Option and documents None for a channel absent from the layout, and ChannelAssignment::Fm(n) is never validated against the layout, so an existing Fm(5) track is neither deleted nor crashed; what changes is the roster offered to new projects and in AddTrackDialog. Added the missing invariant guard (FM voices + DAC channels <= 6) naming the mismatch in its failure, poisoned red-first by reintroducing the defect: fires with 'advertises 6 FM voices plus 1 DAC channels = 7'. Guard scope is stated in its own doc comment as covering only the profiles it registers, since lib.rs has no shared registry constructor to borrow. STILL OPEN and not touched here: an existing FM6 track still exports, which is F30's double-header defect and F27's playback question.
